r4-quality.finding: BLOCKER. tests/test_spine_rail.py::test_worktree_from_spine_walks_to_the_nearest_agent_work_ancestor cannot pass on Windows. The rewritten test asserts _worktree_from_spine(...) == str(worktree) six times, but the new derivation returns a normcase-FOLDED path while str(tmp_path/'worktree') is unfolded. On Windows normcase lowercases the drive letter, so the two differ for every tmp_path without exception - the drive letter alone guarantees it. Proven by running both copies under ntpath: expected 'C:\Users\Tommy\...\test_Worktree0\worktree', returned 'c:\users\tommy\...\test_worktree0\worktree'. The predecessor test passed there (old impl returned str(agent_work.parent), pathlib-case-preserving), so this diff turns a green Windows test red. The sibling table tests/test_worktree_derivation.py does it correctly via _expected() = normcase(normpath(...)) and passes under the same simulation - so the fix is to use that same construction here. This is the exact hazard the implementer named in Evidence 8 for production consumers and then did not apply to its own test.
